title: Revision of Timeline for Filing Suspicious Transaction Reports

paragraphs.text: Reference is invited to paragraph 5 of circular GZ-AML-2019-01 dated November 5, 2019, which prescribes the timeline for filing Suspicious Transaction Reports. To enable more timely action by law enforcement agencies, it has been decided to shorten the timeline for filing Suspicious Transaction Reports with the Financial Intelligence Unit.

With effect from February 1, 2024, paragraph 5 of circular GZ-AML-2019-01 dated November 5, 2019 on the timeline for filing Suspicious Transaction Reports stands substituted by the text set out in paragraph 3 of this circular, which shall thereafter be read as paragraph 5 of circular GZ-AML-2019-01.

The timeline for filing a Suspicious Transaction Report shall be not later than 5 working days from the date on which the Principal Officer arrives at a conclusion that a transaction, whether cash or non-cash, or a series of transactions, is suspicious.

Timeline for forming suspicion: the Principal Officer shall ensure that every alert generated by the transaction monitoring system is examined and a conclusion on whether the transaction is suspicious is recorded within 30 days of the alert, so that the Suspicious Transaction Report timeline is not defeated by delays in alert review.

The tipping-off prohibition in paragraph 6 of circular GZ-AML-2019-01 remains unchanged: no bank or member of its staff shall disclose to the customer or any third party that a Suspicious Transaction Report has been or is being furnished to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

The revised Suspicious Transaction Report filing timeline of 5 working days shall apply to every case in which the Principal Officer arrives at a conclusion of suspicion on or after February 1, 2024, the effective date of circular GZ-AML-2024-01.
